question: Which of the following physiographic divisions of India has extensive alluvial soil ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The North Indian Plain**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The North Indian Plain** is the physiographic division of India that has extensive alluvial soil.
 
• The alluvial soil in the North Indian Plain is primarily deposited by rivers like the Ganges, Yamuna, and their tributaries.
 
• This soil is highly fertile and suitable for the cultivation of crops such as wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.
 
• The North Indian Plain stretches across several states, including Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial soil** is formed by the deposition of sediments brought down by rivers.
 
• It is rich in nutrients such as phosphoric acid, potash, and lime, which are essential for plant growth.
 
• The North Indian Plain is also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plain, highlighting its formation through the alluvial deposits of the Indus and Ganges river systems.
 
• Due to its fertility and favorable climate, the North Indian Plain is one of the most densely populated regions in India.
